cards.text: David is at Hebron when ALL the tribes of Israel show up at once. Every single tribe! The biggest crowd I ever got in that junk drawer was one scared can opener sliding in.

cards.question: The tribes of Israel have come to David at Hebron. How do they describe themselves to him?

cards.text: Then they bring up the old days. Even back when Saul was king over them, David was the one leading Israel out and bringing them back.

cards.question: The tribes remind David what the LORD told him: David would ___ His people Israel and be ruler over them.

cards.text: So the elders of Israel come to King David at Hebron, and he makes a covenant with them before the LORD. Not a handshake, not a thumbs-up in the group chat, a COVENANT!

cards.question: After King David makes a covenant with the elders of Israel at Hebron, what do the elders do?

answers.text: Make him commander of the army
Bring him the crown of Saul

cards.question: David is thirty years old when he becomes king.

cards.text: And David reigns FORTY years, starting with seven years and six months over Judah in Hebron. Friend, I couldn't keep one stamp sharp for forty years!

cards.question: After Hebron, David reigns thirty-three years over all Israel and Judah. From which city?

cards.text: One little problem: Jerusalem isn't David's yet. When David and his men march against the Jebusites who live there, the Jebusites have something to say.

cards.question: David and his men march on Jerusalem. What do the Jebusites tell David?

answers.text: Even the blind and lame can repel you
Pay us and we will open the gates
Our king will come out to meet you

cards.text: They're SO sure, they even think it to themselves: "David cannot get in here." Friend, I said the exact same thing about anybody ever getting me out of that junk drawer.

cards.question: Nevertheless, David captures the fortress of ___, also known as the City of ___.

cards.text: On that day, David tells his men how they're going to reach the Jebusites.

cards.question: What does David say whoever attacks the Jebusites must use?

cards.text: That's why people say, "The blind and the lame will never enter the palace." Then David moves into the fortress, calls it the City of David, and builds it up all the way around, from the supporting terraces inward.

cards.question: David becomes greater and greater. What reason does the passage give?

answers.text: The LORD God of Hosts was with him
Saul's family made peace with him

cards.text: Hiram, king of Tyre, sends envoys to David with cedar logs, carpenters and stonemasons. That's not a housewarming gift, friend, that's a WHOLE construction crew!

cards.question: Hiram's carpenters and stonemasons build a ___ for David.
David realizes the LORD has established him as king and exalted his kingdom for David's own sake.

cards.text: After arriving from Hebron, David takes more concubines and wives from Jerusalem, and more sons and daughters are born to him. The passage names eleven children born to him in Jerusalem, and two of those names are Nathan and Solomon.

findings.problem: The passage starts in the middle of the story ("Then all the tribes..."), but the opening card gives no context for why the tribes come to David at Hebron. It never says that Saul is gone or that David is already reigning over Judah at Hebron. One of its three sentences goes to the joke instead.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on. If the passage starts in the middle of a thought, it gives the context.

findings.problem: David appears for the first time in this lesson and is never introduced. Saul, on card 3, is at least described as having been king.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: "Show up at once" adds a time detail. 2 Samuel 5:1 says only that all the tribes came to David at Hebron. It does not say they came at the same moment.

rule.text: Times stay true. No time in the text means none added.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to supply the exact word of the LORD's line in 5:2 ("You will shepherd My people Israel"). The baker hasn't seen that wording, and nothing earlier points to "shepherd" over "gather" or "teach." The question should ask about meaning the baker can reason out.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The comparison doesn't match the core action. The Jebusites are confidently sure an attacker can't get IN. Papa Dorin's drawer line is about being sure nobody would get him OUT. "The exact same thing" also isn't true, so the joke doesn't click.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: "David tells his men" names an audience the text doesn't give. 2 Samuel 5:8 says only "he said."

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: "That's why people say..." points back to something the baker was never told. No card tells the rest of David's words in 5:8 ("to reach the lame and blind who are despised by David"). Without that, the saying about the blind and the lame has no clear link to anything, and an important detail of 5:8 is missing from the walkthrough.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: The card packs in more than two things happening: the saying about the blind and the lame, David moving into the fortress and naming it, and David building it up all the way around.

rule.text: Aim for one beat per story card. Two is the most. If a story card has more than two things happening, split it.

findings.problem: "What reason does the passage give?" sounds like a test question about the text, not Papa Dorin pausing mid-story.

rule.text: Ask from inside the passage, the way a storyteller pauses to let the listener lean in. The question comes out of the moment Papa Dorin just set up.
